ko.title: [소매업 개론 #8] 6개월 전 누군가가 그 선반의 모든 것을 선택했다

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > 상품화(Merchandising)는 매장에서 무엇을 팔지, 얼마나 취급할지, 언제 구매할지를 결정하는 업무이며, 이러한 결정은 당신이 매장에 들어오기 훨씬 전에 이루어집니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: 어떤 매장에 들어가든 당신은 서로 연결된 세 가지 업무의 결과물을 보고 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **구색(Assortment)**은 매장에서 취급하는 *품목*입니다.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: 두 가지 다이얼이 이를 제어합니다.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **폭(Breadth)**(다양성이라고도 함)은 얼마나 많은 종류의 카테고리나 브랜드를 제공하는지입니다. 즉, 매장에서 땅콩버터뿐만 아니라 엔진 오일, 양말도 파는가 하는 것입니다.

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **깊이(Depth)**는 한 카테고리 *내부*에서 얼마나 많은 선택지를 제공하는지입니다. 예를 들어 크리미, 크런치, 천연, 유기농, 저을 필요 없는 제품 등을 각각 세 가지 용량으로 제공하는 식입니다.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: 모든 소매업체는 이 두 다이얼의 특정 지점을 선택하며, 그 지점이 바로 그 매장의 정체성*입니다.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: 창고형 할인점은 의도적으로 깊이가 얕습니다.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: 전문 러닝화 매장은 의도적으로 폭이 좁지만 매우 깊습니다.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: 계산의 단위는 **SKU**(재고 관리 단위)입니다. 이는 특정 사이즈, 색상, 맛을 가진 하나의 구체적인 품목을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: 16온스 크리미와 16온스 크런치는 하나가 아니라 두 개의 SKU입니다.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **상품 계획(Merchandise planning)**은 *얼마나* 그리고 *언제*에 관한 것입니다.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: 기획자는 카테고리별, 월별 매출을 예측한 다음, 필요한 재고 수준과 그에 따라 사용할 수 있는 예산을 역산합니다.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: 전형적인 통제 도구는 **오픈 투 바이(OTB, Open-to-buy)**입니다. 이는 바이어가 이번 기간에 여전히 집행할 수 있는 금액을 의미합니다:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.src: + Planned sales
segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.src: - Beginning inventory
segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.src: - Merchandise already on order
segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: 만약 그 숫자가 0이라면, 아무리 좋은 거래처럼 보여도 바이어는 구매를 중단합니다.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: 그것이 이 도구의 핵심 목적입니다.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **구매(Buying)**는 실행 단계입니다. 공급업체 선정, 비용 및 결제 조건 협상, 주문 수량 및 배송일 설정, 그리고 내셔널 브랜드와 소매업체 자체 **PB 상품(private label)** 간의 비중을 결정하는 일입니다.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: 바이어는 보통 매출만으로 평가받지 않고 두 가지 숫자로 평가받습니다:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI("재고 투자에 대한 매출 총이익률")는 실제로 중요한 질문에 답합니다. 재고에 묶인 1달러당 몇 달러의 매출 총이익이 돌아왔는가?

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: 1년에 8번 팔리는 20% 마진 상품이 2번 팔리는 45% 마진 상품을 이길 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: 마진만 보는 것은 절반의 답일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활에서

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: 두 번의 장보기 상황을 비교해 봅시다.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: 미국의 일반적인 슈퍼마켓(Kroger, Safeway, 대형 매장 등)에서 땅콩버터 매대는 40피트 길이에 60개 이상의 SKU가 있을 수 있습니다. Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, 자체 브랜드, 유기농 옵션 3가지, 가루형 땅콩버터, 그리고 12가지 용량 등이 있습니다.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: 폭이 넓고* 깊이도 깊습니다.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: 매장은 약속을 하는 것입니다: 당신이 무엇을 찾으러 왔든, 우리는 그것을 가지고 있습니다.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: 트레이더 조(Trader Joe's)에서는 같은 장보기 상황에서 몇 가지 옵션만 제공하며, 대부분 자체 브랜드입니다.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: 이 체인점은 전사적으로 수천 개의 SKU만 취급하는 반면, 대형 슈퍼마켓은 수만 개의 SKU를 취급합니다.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: 이는 간과한 것이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: SKU가 적다는 것은 품목당 주문량이 많아지고, 단위당 비용이 개선되며, 회전율이 빨라지고, 잘 팔리지 않는 상품에 낭비되는 선반 공간이 줄어들며, 쇼핑객이 45분이 아닌 20분 만에 쇼핑을 마칠 수 있다는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: 어느 쪽이 "옳은" 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: 그들은 같은 두 다이얼에 대해 서로 다른 베팅을 하고 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: 그리고 당신은 계획 달력을 실시간으로 확인할 수 있습니다. 7월에 나타나는 신학기용 매대 끝 진열대(endcaps)는 지난 가을에 작성된 예측을 바탕으로 **2월**에 구매된 것입니다.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: 노동절 연휴에 배낭이 60% 할인된 것을 본다면, 그것은 **마크다운(markdown)**을 보고 있는 것입니다. 기획자의 예측이 너무 높았고, 매장은 휴가철을 위해 OTB 예산을 확보하고자 악성 재고를 현금으로 전환하고 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. 구색은 폭(카테고리 수)과 깊이(카테고리당 선택지 수)의 곱이며, 그 조합이 어떤 소매업체인지를 정의합니다.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. 상품 계획은 매출 예측을 재고 계획과 바이어가 집행할 수 있는 금액을 제한하는 오픈 투 바이 예산으로 전환합니다.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. 바이어는 매출 총이익률만으로 평가받지 않고 GMROI와 회전율로 성과를 냅니다. 회전율이 빠르고 마진이 낮은 상품이 마진은 높지만 회전이 느린 상품보다 더 많은 수익을 낼 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: (O/X)** "Depth" refers to the number of different product categories a store carries.
segments.tr: (O/X)** "깊이(Depth)"는 매장이 취급하는 서로 다른 제품 카테고리의 수를 의미한다.

segments.src: **2.** A buyer finds a great closeout deal in October, but the department's open-to-buy for the period is already $0.
segments.tr: **2.** 바이어가 10월에 훌륭한 재고 정리(closeout) 상품을 발견했지만, 해당 기간 부서의 오픈 투 바이(OTB) 예산은 이미 $0입니다.

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: 이것은 무엇을 의미합니까?

segments.src: - (A) The deal is free, since closeouts don't count against the budget
segments.tr: - (A) 재고 정리 상품은 예산에 포함되지 않으므로 공짜이다

segments.src: - (B) The planned inventory and on-order commitments already consume the budget, so no further dollars are available
segments.tr: - (B) 계획된 재고와 이미 주문된 물량이 예산을 모두 소진했으므로, 추가로 사용할 수 있는 금액이 없다

segments.src: - (C) The department has no cash in the bank
segments.tr: - (C) 부서에 은행 잔고가 없다

segments.src: - (D) The buyer must mark down existing stock before ordering anything
segments.tr: - (D) 바이어는 무엇이든 주문하기 전에 기존 재고를 마크다운해야 한다

segments.src: **3.** Product A: 45% gross margin, turns 2x per year.
segments.tr: **3.** 제품 A: 매출 총이익률 45%, 연간 회전율 2회.

segments.src: Product B: 20% gross margin, turns 8x per year.
segments.tr: 제품 B: 매출 총이익률 20%, 연간 회전율 8회.

segments.src: Which generally returns more per dollar of inventory invested?
segments.tr: 일반적으로 투자된 재고 1달러당 더 많은 수익을 돌려주는 것은 무엇인가?

segments.src: - (A) Product A, because margin percentage is higher
segments.tr: - (A) 제품 A, 마진율이 더 높기 때문에

segments.src: - (B) Product B, because turnover more than offsets the lower margin
segments.tr: - (B) 제품 B, 회전율이 낮은 마진을 상쇄하고도 남기 때문에

segments.src: - (C) They are identical
segments.tr: - (C) 동일하다

segments.src: - (D) Cannot be compared without knowing the retail price
segments.tr: - (D) 소매 가격을 모르면 비교할 수 없다

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **SKU (stock keeping unit):** One specific sellable item — a single size, color, and flavor combination.
segments.tr: - **SKU (stock keeping unit):** 판매 가능한 하나의 구체적인 품목. 단일 사이즈, 색상, 맛의 조합.

segments.src: - **Assortment breadth vs. depth:** Breadth = number of different categories or brands carried; depth = number of choices within one category.
segments.tr: - **구색의 폭 vs. 깊이:** 폭 = 취급하는 서로 다른 카테고리나 브랜드의 수; 깊이 = 한 카테고리 내의 선택지 수.

segments.src: - **Open-to-buy (OTB):** The dollar amount a buyer may still commit in a period after accounting for planned sales, planned ending inventory, and merchandise already on order.
segments.tr: - **오픈 투 바이 (OTB):** 계획된 매출, 계획된 기말 재고, 이미 주문된 상품을 고려한 후 바이어가 특정 기간에 여전히 집행할 수 있는 금액.

segments.src: - **GMROI:** Gross margin dollars divided by average inventory cost — margin dollars earned per dollar of inventory investment.
segments.tr: - **GMROI:** 매출 총이익을 평균 재고 원가로 나눈 값. 재고 투자 1달러당 벌어들인 매출 총이익.

segments.src: - **Markdown:** A permanent reduction in retail price used to clear inventory that is selling below plan.
segments.tr: - **마크다운 (Markdown):** 계획보다 판매가 저조한 재고를 처리하기 위해 소매 가격을 영구적으로 인하하는 것.

segments.src: - **Private label:** Merchandise sold under the retailer's own brand, typically at lower cost and higher margin than comparable national brands.
segments.tr: - **PB 상품 (Private label):** 소매업체 자체 브랜드로 판매되는 상품. 일반적으로 유사한 내셔널 브랜드보다 원가는 낮고 마진은 높음.

zh.title: [零售学 101 #8] 六个月前有人选定了货架上的所有东西

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > 商品营销是决定门店销售什么、销售多少以及何时采购的工作——这些决定早在你走进来之前就已经做出了。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: 走进任何一家门店，你看到的都是三项相互关联工作的成果。

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **商品组合**是门店销售*什么*。

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: 两个维度控制它。

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **宽度**（也称品种）是你提供多少不同的类别或品牌——门店是否销售花生酱，也销售机油，也销售袜子？

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **深度**是你在*一个*类别内提供多少选择——细腻的、脆的、天然的、有机的、免搅拌的，各有三种尺寸。

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: 每家零售商都在这两个维度上选择一个位置，这个位置*就是*门店的身份。

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: 仓储俱乐部有意设置浅深度。

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: 专业跑步店有意设置窄但很深。

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: 计数单位是**SKU**（库存单位）——一个特定尺寸、颜色和口味的特定商品。

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: 细腻型 16 盎司和脆型 16 盎司是两个 SKU，而不是一个。

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **商品规划**是*多少*和*何时*。

segments.tr: 规划师按类别按月份预测销售，然后倒推需要有多少库存，因此有多少美元可用于支出。

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: 经典的控制工具是**可购额（OTB）**——采购员在本期仍被允许承诺的美元金额：

segments.tr: 如果这个数字是零，采购员停止采购，无论交易看起来多么划算。

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: 这就是这个工具的全部意义。

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **采购**是执行：选择供应商、协商成本和付款条款、设定订单数量和交货日期，以及决定多少份额分配给国家品牌对比零售商自有**自有品牌**。

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:

segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI（"库存投资毛利回报率"）回答真正重要的问题：库存中每投入一美元，能获得多少毛利美元回报？

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: 年销售八次的 20% 毛利商品可以超越年销售两次的 45% 毛利商品。

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: 仅毛利是不完整的答案。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: 比较两次食品杂货购物。

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: 在传统的美国超市——Kroger、Safeway、大型门店——花生酱区域可能长达 40 英尺，有 60 多个 SKU：Jif、Skippy、Peter Pan、门店品牌、三种有机选项、粉状花生酱以及十多种尺寸。

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: 既宽*又*深。

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: 门店做出承诺：无论你来找什么，我们都有。

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: 在 Trader Joe's，相同的购物给你一小部分选项，大多是他们自有品牌。

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: 该连锁公司范围内只销售几千个 SKU，而全尺寸超市销售数万个。

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: 那不是疏忽。

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: 较少的 SKU 意味着每件商品订单更大、单位成本更好、周转更快、慢销商品浪费的货架空间更少，购物者在门店中花费 20 分钟而不是 45 分钟。

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: 两者都不是"对的"。

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: 它们是对相同两个维度的不同押注。

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: 你可以实时观看规划日历：7 月出现的返校尾端陈列在**2 月**购买，基于前一年秋季编写的预测。

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: 当你在劳动节周末看到背包打 60% 折扣时，你看到的是一次**降价**——规划师的估计太高了，门店正在将死库存转换回现金，以便 OTB 为假日补充。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. 商品组合是宽度（多少类别）乘以深度（每个类别多少选择）——这种混合定义了你是什么类型的零售商。

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. 商品规划将销售预测转变为库存计划和可购额预算，限定采购员可以承诺的内容。

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. 采购员通过 GMROI 和周转赢利，而不是仅毛利——快速、低毛利商品可以超越缓慢、高毛利商品。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **SKU (stock keeping unit):** One specific sellable item — a single size, color, and flavor combination.
segments.tr: - **SKU（库存单位）：** 一个特定的可销售商品——单一尺寸、颜色和口味组合。

segments.src: - **Assortment breadth vs. depth:** Breadth = number of different categories or brands carried; depth = number of choices within one category.
segments.tr: - **商品组合宽度对比深度：** 宽度 = 销售的不同类别或品牌的数量；深度 = 一个类别内的选择数量。

segments.src: - **Open-to-buy (OTB):** The dollar amount a buyer may still commit in a period after accounting for planned sales, planned ending inventory, and merchandise already on order.
segments.tr: - **可购额（OTB）：** 采购员在一个期间内，在考虑计划销售、计划期末库存和已订购商品后，仍然可以承诺的美元金额。

segments.src: - **GMROI:** Gross margin dollars divided by average inventory cost — margin dollars earned per dollar of inventory investment.
segments.tr: - **GMROI：** 毛利美元除以平均库存成本——每投入库存美元获得的毛利美元。

segments.src: - **Markdown:** A permanent reduction in retail price used to clear inventory that is selling below plan.
segments.tr: - **降价：** 零售价永久降低，用于清理销售低于计划的库存。

segments.src: - **Private label:** Merchandise sold under the retailer's own brand, typically at lower cost and higher margin than comparable national brands.
segments.tr: - **自有品牌：** 在零售商自有品牌下销售的商品，通常成本更低、毛利比可比国家品牌更高。

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > व्यापार वह काम है जो यह तय करता है कि एक दुकान क्या बेचती है, इसमें कितना रखना है, और इसे कब खरीदना है — और ये फैसले बहुत पहले लिए गए थे इससे पहले कि आप अंदर आएं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: किसी भी दुकान में जाएं और आप तीन जुड़े हुए कामों का नतीजा देख रहे हैं।

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **व्यवस्थापन** वह है जो दुकान रखती है।

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: दो डायल इसे नियंत्रित करते हैं।

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **चौड़ाई** (जिसे विविधता भी कहते हैं) यह है कि आप कितने विभिन्न श्रेणियों या ब्रांडों की पेशकश करते हैं — क्या दुकान मूंगफली का मक्खन बेचती है, और मोटर ऑयल भी, और मोजे भी?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **गहराई** यह है कि आप एक श्रेणी के *अंदर* कितने विकल्प प्रदान करते हैं — क्रीमी, कुरकुरा, प्राकृतिक, जैविक, नो-स्टिर, तीन आकार में प्रत्येक।

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: हर खुदरा विक्रेता उन दोनों डायलों पर एक बिंदु चुनता है, और वह बिंदु दुकान की पहचान *है*।

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: एक गोदाम क्लब जानबूझकर उथला है।

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: एक विशेष रनिंग दुकान जानबूझकर संकीर्ण लेकिन बहुत गहरी है।

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: गिना जाने वाली इकाई **SKU** (स्टॉक कीपिंग यूनिट) है — एक विशिष्ट वस्तु एक विशिष्ट आकार, रंग, और स्वाद में।

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: क्रीमी 16 oz और कुरकुरा 16 oz दो SKU हैं, एक नहीं।

segments.tr: कम SKU का मतलब है प्रति वस्तु बड़े ऑर्डर, प्रति यूनिट बेहतर लागत, तेजी से बदलाव, धीमी चलने वाली चीजों पर बर्बाद कम शेल्फ स्थान, और एक खरीदार जो 45 के बजाय दुकान में 20 मिनट बिताता है।

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: कोई भी "सही" नहीं है।

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: वे एक ही दो डायलों पर विभिन्न दांव हैं।

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: और आप वास्तविक समय में योजना कैलेंडर देख सकते हैं: जुलाई में दिखाई देने वाले स्कूल वापसी एंडकैप को **फरवरी** में खरीदा गया था, पिछली गिरावट में लिखे गए पूर्वानुमान से।

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: जब आप लेबर डे सप्ताहांत पर 60% छूट पर बैकपैक देखते हैं, तो आप एक **मार्कडाउन** देख रहे हैं — योजनाकार का अनुमान बहुत अधिक था, और दुकान मृत इन्वेंटरी को नकद में परिवर्तित कर रही है ताकि OTB छुट्टी के लिए भर जाए।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. व्यवस्थापन चौड़ाई है (कितनी श्रेणियां) गुणा गहराई (प्रति श्रेणी कितने विकल्प) — वह मिश्रण परिभाषित करता है कि आप किस तरह के खुदरा विक्रेता हैं।

segments.src: - **Assortment breadth vs. depth:** Breadth = number of different categories or brands carried; depth = number of choices within one category.
segments.tr: - **व्यवस्थापन चौड़ाई बनाम गहराई:** चौड़ाई = विभिन्न श्रेणियों या ब्रांडों की संख्या; गहराई = एक श्रेणी के भीतर विकल्पों की संख्या।

segments.src: - **Open-to-buy (OTB):** The dollar amount a buyer may still commit in a period after accounting for planned sales, planned ending inventory, and merchandise already on order.
segments.tr: - **खुली-खरीद (OTB):** डॉलर की राशि जो एक खरीदार योजित बिक्री, योजित अंतिम इन्वेंटरी, और पहले से ही ऑर्डर किए गए व्यापार को ध्यान में रखने के बाद अवधि में प्रतिबद्ध हो सकता है।

segments.src: - **GMROI:** Gross margin dollars divided by average inventory cost — margin dollars earned per dollar of inventory investment.

segments.src: - **Markdown:** A permanent reduction in retail price used to clear inventory that is selling below plan.

segments.src: - **Private label:** Merchandise sold under the retailer's own brand, typically at lower cost and higher margin than comparable national brands.

es.title: [Retailing 101 #8] Alguien Eligió Todo lo que hay en ese Estante hace Seis Meses

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > El merchandising es el trabajo de decidir qué vende una tienda, cuánto inventario mantener y cuándo comprar — y esas decisiones se tomaron mucho antes de que entraras.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: Entra a cualquier tienda y estás viendo el resultado de tres trabajos conectados.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **Surtido** es *qué* vende la tienda.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: Dos controles lo regulan.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **Amplitud** (también llamada variedad) es cuántas categorías o marcas diferentes ofreces — ¿la tienda vende mantequilla de maní, y también aceite de motor, y también calcetines?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **Profundidad** es cuántas opciones ofreces *dentro* de una categoría — cremosa, crujiente, natural, orgánica, sin mezclar, en tres tamaños cada una.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: Cada minorista elige un punto en esos dos controles, y ese punto *es* la identidad de la tienda.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: Un club de almacén es deliberadamente superficial.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: Una tienda especializada en running es deliberadamente estrecha pero muy profunda.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: La unidad contabilizada es la **SKU** (unidad de mantenimiento de inventario) — un artículo específico en un tamaño, color y sabor específicos.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: Cremosa 16 oz y crujiente 16 oz son dos SKUs, no una.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **Planificación de mercancía** es *cuánto* y *cuándo*.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: Un planificador pronostica ventas por categoría por mes, luego trabaja hacia atrás para determinar cuánto inventario debe estar disponible, y por lo tanto cuántos dólares están disponibles para gastar.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: La herramienta de control clásica es **compra disponible (OTB)** — los dólares que un comprador aún puede comprometer en este período:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.src: + Planned sales
segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.src: - Beginning inventory
segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.src: - Merchandise already on order
segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: Si ese número es cero, el comprador deja de comprar, sin importar cuán bueno se vea el trato.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: Ese es el punto completo de la herramienta.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **Compra** es la ejecución: elegir proveedores, negociar costos y términos de pago, establecer cantidades de pedido y fechas de entrega, y decidir qué parte se asigna a marcas nacionales versus la **marca propia** del minorista.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: Los compradores generalmente se juzgan por dos números en lugar de solo las ventas:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI ("retorno de margen bruto en inversión de inventario") responde la pregunta que realmente importa: por cada dólar inmovilizado en inventario, ¿cuántos dólares de margen bruto regresaron?

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: Un artículo con margen del 20% que se vende ocho veces al año puede superar a un artículo con margen del 45% que se vende dos veces.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: El margen por sí solo es una respuesta incompleta.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: Compara dos viajes de compras de abarrotes.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: En un supermercado convencional de EE. UU. — un Kroger, un Safeway, una tienda de gran formato — el conjunto de mantequilla de maní podría ocupar 40 pies con más de 60 SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, la marca de la tienda, tres opciones orgánicas, mantequilla de maní en polvo, y una docena de tamaños.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: Amplio *y* profundo.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: La tienda está haciendo una promesa: sea lo que sea que viniste a buscar, lo tenemos.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: En Trader Joe's, el mismo viaje te da un puñado de opciones, principalmente su propia marca.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: La cadena lleva solo unos pocos miles de SKUs en toda la empresa, mientras que un supermercado de tamaño completo lleva decenas de miles.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: Eso no es una omisión.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: Menos SKUs significa pedidos más grandes por artículo, mejor costo por unidad, rotación más rápida, menos espacio en el estante desperdiciado en artículos lentos, y un cliente que pasa 20 minutos en la tienda en lugar de 45.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: Ninguno es "correcto".

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: Son apuestas diferentes en los mismos dos controles.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: Y puedes ver el calendario de planificación en tiempo real: los expositores de regreso a clases que aparecen en julio se compraron en **febrero**, de un pronóstico escrito el otoño anterior.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: Cuando ves mochilas con descuento del 60% el fin de semana del Día del Trabajo, estás viendo una **rebaja** — la estimación del planificador fue demasiado alta, y la tienda está convirtiendo inventario muerto en efectivo para que el OTB se reponga para las vacaciones.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de Tres Líneas

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. El surtido es amplitud (cuántas categorías) multiplicado por profundidad (cuántas opciones por categoría) — esa combinación define qué tipo de minorista eres.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. La planificación de mercancía convierte un pronóstico de ventas en un plan de inventario y un presupuesto de compra disponible que limita lo que el comprador puede comprometer.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. Los compradores ganan en GMROI y rotación, no en margen bruto solo — un artículo rápido de margen delgado puede ganar más que uno lento de margen grueso.

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > البضاعة هي وظيفة تحديد ما يبيعه المتجر، وكم عدد ما يتعين عليه حمله، وموعد شراؤه — وتم اتخاذ القرارات قبل وقت طويل من دخولك.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## المفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: ادخل أي متجر وأنت تنظر إلى ناتج ثلاث وظائف مترابطة.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **التشكيلة** هي *ما* يحمله المتجر.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: هناك مؤشران يسيطران عليها.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **الاتساع** (يُسمى أيضاً التنوع) هو عدد الفئات أو العلامات التجارية المختلفة التي تقدمها — هل يبيع المتجر زبدة الفول السوداني، وأيضاً زيت المحرك، وأيضاً الجوارب؟

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **العمق** هو عدد الخيارات التي تقدمها *داخل* فئة واحدة — كريمي، مقرمش، طبيعي، عضوي، بدون تقليب، في ثلاثة أحجام لكل منها.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: كل بائع تجزئة يختار نقطة على هذين المؤشرين، وتلك النقطة *هي* هوية المتجر.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: نادي المستودع متعمد الضحالة.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: متجر المتخصص للركض متعمد الضيق لكن عميق جداً.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: الوحدة المحسوبة هي **SKU** (وحدة الحفاظ على المخزون) — عنصر واحد محدد في حجم وحدة لون وطعم محدد واحد.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: كريمي 16 أونصة ومقرمش 16 أونصة هما اثنين من وحدات حفظ المخزون، وليسا واحداً.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **تخطيط البضاعة** هو *كم* و*متى*.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: يقوم المخطط بالتنبؤ بالمبيعات حسب الفئة شهرياً، ثم يعود بالحسابات للخلف لمعرفة مقدار المخزون الذي يجب أن يكون في المتناول، وبالتالي عدد الدولارات المتاحة للإنفاق.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: الأداة التحكم الكلاسيكية هي **الفتح للشراء (OTB)** — الدولارات التي لا يزال يُسمح للمشتري بالالتزام بها في هذه الفترة:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: إذا كان هذا الرقم صفراً، يتوقف المشتري عن الشراء، بغض النظر عن مدى جودة العرض.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: هذا هو الهدف برمته من الأداة.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **الشراء** هو التنفيذ: اختيار البائعين، والتفاوض على التكلفة وشروط الدفع، وتحديد كميات الطلب وتواريخ التسليم، وتقرير ما تذهب حصته للعلامات التجارية الوطنية مقابل **العلامة التجارية الخاصة** للبائع بالتجزئة.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: عادة ما يتم الحكم على المشترين بناءً على رقمين بدلاً من المبيعات وحدها:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI ("العائد على هامش الربح على استثمار المخزون") يجيب على السؤال الذي يهم فعلاً: مقابل كل دولار مرتبط بالمخزون، كم عدد دولارات هامش الربح التي عادت؟

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: عنصر بهامش 20٪ يُباع ثماني مرات في السنة يمكن أن يتفوق على عنصر بهامش 45٪ يُباع مرتين.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: الهامش وحده نصف إجابة فقط.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: قارن بين رحلتي تسوق بقالة.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: في سوبرماركت أمريكي تقليدي — كروجر، سيفوي، متجر بتنسيق كبير — قد تمتد مجموعة زبدة الفول السوداني 40 قدماً بـ 60 وحدة حفظ مخزون أو أكثر: Jif، Skippy، Peter Pan، العلامة التجارية للمتجر، ثلاث خيارات عضوية، زبدة الفول السوداني المسحوقة، وعشرات الأحجام.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: واسعة *و* عميقة.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: المتجر يقدم وعداً: مهما جئت من أجله، لدينا.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: في Trader Joe's، توفر نفس الرحلة لك حفنة من الخيارات، معظمها من علامتهم التجارية الخاصة.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: تحمل السلسلة آلاف قليلة فقط من وحدات حفظ المخزون على مستوى الشركة، بينما يحمل السوبرماركت كامل الحجم عشرات الآلاف.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: هذا ليس إغفالاً.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: وحدات حفظ مخزون أقل تعني طلبات أكبر لكل عنصر، تكلفة أقل لكل وحدة، أدوار أسرع، أقل مساحة رفوف مهدرة على البطء، والتاجر الذي ينفق 20 دقيقة في المتجر بدلاً من 45.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: لا أحد منهما "صحيح."

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: إنها رهانات مختلفة على نفس المؤشرين.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: ويمكنك مراقبة تقويم التخطيط في الوقت الفعلي: نهايات عرض العودة إلى المدرسة التي تظهر في يوليو تم شراؤها في **فبراير**، من توقع مكتوب في الخريف السابق.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: عندما ترى حقائب الظهر بخصم 60٪ في نهاية أسبوع يوم العمل، أنت ترى **تخفيض السعر** — كان تقدير المخطط مرتفعاً جداً، والمتجر يحول المخزون الميت إلى نقود بحيث يعاد ملء OTB للعطلة.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. التشكيلة هي الاتساع (عدد الفئات) مضروباً في العمق (عدد الخيارات لكل فئة) — أن هذا المزيج يحدد نوع بائع التجزئة الذي تكونه.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. تحويل تخطيط البضاعة توقع المبيعات إلى خطة مخزون وميزانية فتح للشراء تحد ما يمكن للمشتري الالتزام به.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. يفوز المشترون على GMROI والدوران، وليس على هامش الربح الإجمالي وحده — يمكن لعنصر سريع بهامش رقيق أن يكسب أكثر من واحد بطيء بهامش دهني.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: La chaîne ne propose que quelques milliers de SKU à l'échelle de l'entreprise, là où un supermarché de taille normale en transporte des dizaines de milliers.

segments.tr: Ce n'est pas une inadvertance.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: Quand vous voyez des sacs à dos à 60 % de réduction le week-end de la Fête du Travail, vous voyez une **réduction de prix** — l'estimation du planificateur était trop élevée, et le magasin convertit les stocks invendus en trésorerie pour reconstituer l'OTB pour les vacances.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. La planification des marchandises transforme une prévision de ventes en plan d'inventaire et en budget d'open-to-buy qui plafonne ce que l'acheteur peut engager.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. Les acheteurs gagnent sur le GMROI et la rotation, pas sur la seule marge brute — un article rapide à faible marge peut surpasser un article lent à marge élevée.

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: Entre em qualquer loja e você está vendo o resultado de três trabalhos conectados.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **Sortimento** é *o que* a loja oferece.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: Dois controles o governam.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **Amplitude** (também chamada de variedade) é quantas categorias ou marcas diferentes você oferece — a loja vende manteiga de amendoim, e também óleo de motor, e também meias?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **Profundidade** é quantas opções você oferece *dentro* de uma categoria — cremosa, crocante, natural, orgânica, sem mexer, em três tamanhos cada.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: Todo varejista escolhe um ponto nesses dois controles, e esse ponto *é* a identidade da loja.

segments.tr: Um clube de depósito é deliberadamente raso.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: Uma loja de corrida especializada é deliberadamente estreita, mas muito profunda.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.

in.title: [Retailing 101 #8] Seseorang Memilih Semua Produk di Rak Itu Enam Bulan Lalu

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > Merchandising adalah pekerjaan untuk memutuskan apa yang dijual toko, berapa banyak yang disimpan, dan kapan membelinya — dan keputusan itu dibuat jauh sebelum Anda masuk.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: Masuk ke toko mana pun dan Anda melihat hasil dari tiga pekerjaan yang terhubung.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **Assortment** adalah *apa* yang dijual toko.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: Dua dial mengontrolnya.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **Breadth** (juga disebut variety) adalah berapa banyak kategori atau brand berbeda yang Anda tawarkan — apakah toko menjual selai kacang, juga minyak motor, dan juga kaus kaki?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **Depth** adalah berapa banyak pilihan yang Anda tawarkan *di dalam* satu kategori — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, masing-masing dalam tiga ukuran.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: Setiap pengecer memilih titik pada kedua dial itu, dan titik itu *adalah* identitas toko.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: Klub gudang sengaja memiliki kedalaman rendah.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: Toko sepatu khusus sengaja sempit tetapi sangat dalam.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: Unit yang dihitung adalah **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — satu item spesifik dalam ukuran, warna, dan rasa tertentu.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: Creamy 16 oz dan crunchy 16 oz adalah dua SKU, bukan satu.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **Merchandise planning** adalah *berapa banyak* dan *kapan*.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: Seorang planner memperkirakan penjualan per kategori per bulan, kemudian bekerja mundur untuk menentukan berapa banyak inventory yang harus tersedia, dan karenanya berapa banyak dollar yang tersedia untuk dibelanjakan.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: Alat kontrol klasik adalah **open-to-buy (OTB)** — dollar yang masih diperbolehkan dibeli oleh pembeli dalam periode ini:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.src: + Planned sales
segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.src: - Beginning inventory
segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.src: - Merchandise already on order
segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: Jika angka itu nol, pembeli berhenti membeli, tidak peduli seberapa baik penawaran itu.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: Itulah seluruh poin dari alat ini.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **Buying** adalah eksekusi: memilih vendor, bernegosiasi biaya dan syarat pembayaran, menetapkan kuantitas pesanan dan tanggal pengiriman, dan memutuskan berapa bagian untuk brand nasional versus **private label** milik pengecer.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: Pembeli biasanya dinilai berdasarkan dua angka daripada penjualan saja:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") menjawab pertanyaan yang benar-benar penting: untuk setiap dollar yang terikat dalam inventory, berapa banyak dollar gross margin yang kembali?

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: Item dengan margin 20% yang terjual delapan kali setahun dapat mengalahkan item dengan margin 45% yang terjual dua kali.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: Margin saja adalah jawaban setengah jalan.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: Bandingkan dua kali berbelanja groceries.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: Di supermarket AS konvensional — Kroger, Safeway, toko format besar — koleksi selai kacang mungkin memanjang 40 kaki dengan 60+ SKU: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, brand toko, tiga pilihan organik, selai kacang bubuk, dan selusin ukuran.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: Luas *dan* dalam.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: Toko membuat janji: apapun yang Anda cari, kami punya.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: Di Trader Joe's, perjalanan yang sama memberi Anda segelintir pilihan, sebagian besar label mereka sendiri.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: Rantai ini membawa hanya beberapa ribu SKU di seluruh perusahaan, sementara supermarket ukuran penuh membawa puluhan ribu.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: Itu bukan kebetulan.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: Lebih sedikit SKU berarti pesanan lebih besar per item, biaya per unit lebih baik, perputaran lebih cepat, ruang rak lebih sedikit terbuang pada slow movers, dan pembeli yang menghabiskan 20 menit di toko daripada 45.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: Keduanya tidak "benar."

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: Mereka adalah taruhan berbeda pada dua dial yang sama.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: Dan Anda dapat melihat kalender perencanaan secara real time: endcap kembali ke sekolah yang muncul di Juli dibeli di **Februari**, dari prakiraan yang ditulis musim gugur sebelumnya.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: Ketika Anda melihat tas punggung dengan diskon 60% pada akhir pekan Labor Day, Anda melihat **markdown** — perkiraan planner terlalu tinggi, dan toko mengonversi inventory mati kembali ke uang tunai sehingga OTB diisi ulang untuk liburan.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. Assortment adalah breadth (berapa banyak kategori) dikali depth (berapa banyak pilihan per kategori) — campuran itu mendefinisikan jenis pengecer apa Anda.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. Merchandise planning mengubah prakiraan penjualan menjadi rencana inventory dan anggaran open-to-buy yang membatasi apa yang dapat dibeli oleh pembeli.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. Pembeli menang pada GMROI dan perputaran, bukan gross margin saja — item dengan margin tipis yang cepat dapat menghasilkan lebih banyak daripada item dengan margin tebal yang lambat.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.tr: (O/X)** "Depth" mengacu pada jumlah kategori produk berbeda yang dibawa toko.

segments.src: **2.** A buyer finds a great closeout deal in October, but the department's open-to-buy for the period is already $0.
segments.tr: **2.** Pembeli menemukan penawaran closeout bagus di Oktober, tetapi open-to-buy departemen untuk periode tersebut sudah $0.

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: Apa artinya itu?

segments.tr: - (A) Penawaran itu gratis, karena closeouts tidak dihitung terhadap anggaran

segments.src: - (B) The planned inventory and on-order commitments already consume the budget, so no further dollars are available
segments.tr: - (B) Inventory yang direncanakan dan komitmen pesanan sudah menghabiskan anggaran, jadi tidak ada dollar lebih lanjut yang tersedia

segments.src: - (C) The department has no cash in the bank
segments.tr: - (C) Departemen tidak memiliki uang tunai di bank

segments.src: - (D) The buyer must mark down existing stock before ordering anything
segments.tr: - (D) Pembeli harus menurunkan harga stok yang ada sebelum memesan apa pun

segments.src: **3.** Product A: 45% gross margin, turns 2x per year.
segments.tr: **3.** Produk A: 45% gross margin, berputar 2x per tahun.

segments.src: Product B: 20% gross margin, turns 8x per year.
segments.tr: Produk B: 20% gross margin, berputar 8x per tahun.

segments.src: Which generally returns more per dollar of inventory invested?
segments.tr: Mana yang umumnya mengembalikan lebih banyak per dollar inventory yang diinvestasikan?

segments.src: - (A) Product A, because margin percentage is higher
segments.tr: - (A) Produk A, karena persentase margin lebih tinggi

segments.src: - (B) Product B, because turnover more than offsets the lower margin
segments.tr: - (B) Produk B, karena perputaran lebih dari mengimbangi margin yang lebih rendah

segments.src: - (C) They are identical
segments.tr: - (C) Mereka identik

segments.src: - (D) Cannot be compared without knowing the retail price
segments.tr: - (D) Tidak dapat dibandingkan tanpa mengetahui harga ritel

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > Merchandising ist die Aufgabe zu entscheiden, was ein Geschäft verkauft, wie viel davon zu führen ist, und wann man es kauft — und diese Entscheidungen wurden lange bevor Sie eintraten, getroffen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das Konzept von heute

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: Betreten Sie ein beliebiges Geschäft und Sie sehen das Ergebnis von drei miteinander verbundenen Aufgaben.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **Sortiment** ist *das*, was das Geschäft führt.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: Zwei Schieberegler steuern es.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **Breite** (auch Vielfalt genannt) ist, wie viele verschiedene Kategorien oder Marken Sie anbieten — verkauft das Geschäft Erdnussbutter, auch Motoröl und auch Socken?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **Tiefe** ist, wie viele Wahlmöglichkeiten Sie *innerhalb* einer Kategorie anbieten — cremig, knusprig, natur, bio, rührfrei, in je drei Größen.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: Jeder Einzelhandelshändler wählt einen Punkt auf diesen beiden Schiebereglern, und dieser Punkt *ist* die Identität des Geschäfts.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: Ein Lagerklubb ist absichtlich flach angelegt.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: Ein spezialisiertes Laufschuhgeschäft ist absichtlich eng, aber sehr tief.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: Die gezählte Einheit ist die **SKU** (Lagerverwaltungseinheit) — ein bestimmter Artikel in einer bestimmten Größe, Farbe und Geschmack.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: Cremig 16 oz und knusprig 16 oz sind zwei SKUs, nicht eine.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **Warenverwaltungsplanung** ist *wie viel* und *wann*.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: Ein Planer prognostiziert Verkäufe nach Kategorie und Monat, arbeitet dann rückwärts, wie viel Bestand verfügbar sein muss, und daher, wie viele Dollar ausgegeben werden können.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: Das klassische Steuertool ist **Open-to-Buy (OTB)** — die Dollar, die ein Käufer in dieser Phase noch binden darf:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.src: + Planned sales
segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.src: - Beginning inventory
segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.src: - Merchandise already on order
segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: Wenn diese Zahl null ist, hört der Käufer auf zu kaufen, egal wie gut das Angebot aussieht.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: Das ist der ganze Sinn des Tools.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **Einkaufen** ist die Ausführung: Lieferanten auswählen, Kosten und Zahlungsbedingungen verhandeln, Bestellmengen und Lieferdaten festlegen, und entscheiden, welcher Anteil zu Nationalmarken gegenüber der eigenen **Handelsmarke** des Einzelhandelshändlers geht.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: Käufer werden normalerweise anhand von zwei Zahlen bewertet, nicht nur anhand des Umsatzes:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI ("Bruttospannenrendite auf Bestandsinvestition") beantwortet die Frage, die wirklich zählt: Für jeden Dollar, der im Bestand gebunden ist, wie viele Bruttospannen-Dollar kamen zurück?

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: Ein 20%-Spannen-Artikel, der achtmal pro Jahr verkauft wird, kann einen 45%-Spannen-Artikel schlagen, der zweimal verkauft wird.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: Die reine Spanne ist eine unvollständige Antwort.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: Vergleichen Sie zwei Einkaufsfahrten zum Supermarkt.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: In einem herkömmlichen US-Supermarkt — einem Kroger, einem Safeway, einem großformatigen Geschäft — könnte die Erdnussbutter-Auswahl 40 Fuß mit 60+ SKUs reichen: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, die Handelsmarke, drei Bio-Optionen, pulverisierte Erdnussbutter und ein Dutzend Größen.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: Breit *und* tief.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: Das Geschäft macht ein Versprechen: Was immer Sie suchten, wir haben es.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: Bei Trader Joe's gibt Ihnen die gleiche Einkaufsfahrt eine Handvoll Optionen, meist ihre eigene Marke.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: Die Kette führt nur wenige tausend SKUs unternehmensausweit, während ein vollständiger Supermarkt zehntausende führt.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: Das ist kein Versehen.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: Weniger SKUs bedeuten größere Bestellungen pro Artikel, bessere Kosten pro Einheit, schnellere Umschläge, weniger Regalboden auf langsame Verkäufer verschwendet, und ein Käufer, der 20 Minuten im Geschäft anstelle von 45 ausgibt.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: Keiner ist "richtig".

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: Es sind unterschiedliche Wetten auf die gleichen zwei Schieberegler.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: Und Sie können den Planungskalender in Echtzeit sehen: die Rück-zum-Schulanfang-Endkappen, die im Juli erscheinen, wurden im **Februar** gekauft, aus einer Vorhersage, die im vorherigen Herbst geschrieben wurde.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: Wenn Sie Rucksäcke mit 60% Rabatt am Labor-Day-Wochenende sehen, sehen Sie einen **Preisnachlass** — die Schätzung des Planers war zu hoch, und das Geschäft konvertiert totes Inventar zurück in Bargeld, damit das OTB für die Feiertage wieder aufgefüllt wird.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. Sortiment ist Breite (wie viele Kategorien) mal Tiefe (wie viele Wahlmöglichkeiten pro Kategorie) — diese Mischung definiert, welche Art von Einzelhandelshändler Sie sind.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. Die Warenverwaltungsplanung verwandelt eine Verkaufsprognose in einen Bestandsplan und ein Open-to-Buy-Budget, das begrenzt, was der Käufer binden kann.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. Käufer gewinnen bei GMROI und Umschlag, nicht nur bei Bruttospanne — ein schnelles, dünneres-Spannen-Artikel kann ein langsames, dicker-Spannen-Artikel übertreffen.

vi.title: [Bán lẻ 101 #8] Ai đó đã chọn mọi thứ trên kệ đó sáu tháng trước

segments.src: > Merchandising is the job of deciding what a store sells, how much of it to carry, and when to buy it — and the decisions were made long before you walked in.
segments.tr: > Merchandising là công việc quyết định cửa hàng bán gì, bao nhiêu sản phẩm để mang theo, và khi nào mua nó — và những quyết định này đã được đưa ra từ lâu trước khi bạn bước vào.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm Hôm nay

segments.src: Walk into any store and you are looking at the output of three linked jobs.
segments.tr: Bước vào bất kỳ cửa hàng nào và bạn đang nhìn vào kết quả của ba công việc liên kết.

segments.src: **Assortment** is *what* the store carries.
segments.tr: **Assortment** là *những gì* cửa hàng bán.

segments.src: Two dials control it.
segments.tr: Hai yếu tố điều khiển nó.

segments.src: **Breadth** (also called variety) is how many different categories or brands you offer — does the store sell peanut butter, and also motor oil, and also socks?
segments.tr: **Breadth** (còn gọi là variety) là có bao nhiêu danh mục hoặc thương hiệu khác nhau bạn cung cấp — cửa hàng có bán bơ lạc, dầu động cơ, và vớ không?

segments.src: **Depth** is how many choices you offer *inside* one category — creamy, crunchy, natural, organic, no-stir, in three sizes each.
segments.tr: **Depth** là có bao nhiêu lựa chọn bạn cung cấp *trong* một danh mục — kem, giòn, tự nhiên, hữu cơ, không cần khuấy, mỗi loại có ba kích cỡ.

segments.src: Every retailer picks a point on those two dials, and that point *is* the store's identity.
segments.tr: Mọi nhà bán lẻ chọn một điểm trên hai yếu tố đó, và điểm đó *là* bản sắc của cửa hàng.

segments.src: A warehouse club is deliberately shallow.
segments.tr: Một kho bán hàng theo hội viên cố ý nông.

segments.src: A specialty running shop is deliberately narrow but very deep.
segments.tr: Một cửa hàng chuyên dụng cho chạy bộ cố ý hẹp nhưng rất sâu.

segments.src: The unit being counted is the **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — one specific item in one specific size, color, and flavor.
segments.tr: Đơn vị được tính là **SKU** (stock keeping unit) — một mặt hàng cụ thể với một kích cỡ, màu sắc, và hương vị cụ thể.

segments.src: Creamy 16 oz and crunchy 16 oz are two SKUs, not one.
segments.tr: Kem 16 oz và giòn 16 oz là hai SKU, không phải một.

segments.src: **Merchandise planning** is *how much* and *when*.
segments.tr: **Merchandise planning** là *bao nhiêu* và *khi nào*.

segments.src: A planner forecasts sales by category by month, then works backward to how much inventory must be on hand, and therefore how many dollars are available to spend.
segments.tr: Một nhà lập kế hoạch dự báo bán hàng theo danh mục theo tháng, sau đó làm việc ngược lại để xác định phải có bao nhiêu hàng tồn kho, và do đó có bao nhiêu đô la có sẵn để chi tiêu.

segments.src: The classic control tool is **open-to-buy (OTB)** — the dollars a buyer is still allowed to commit this period:
segments.tr: Công cụ kiểm soát cổ điển là **open-to-buy (OTB)** — số đô la mà người mua vẫn được phép cam kết trong thời kỳ này:

segments.src: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory
segments.tr: Open-to-buy = Planned end-of-month inventory

segments.src: + Planned sales
segments.tr: + Planned sales

segments.src: + Planned markdowns
segments.tr: + Planned markdowns

segments.src: - Beginning inventory
segments.tr: - Beginning inventory

segments.src: - Merchandise already on order
segments.tr: - Merchandise already on order

segments.src: If that number is zero, the buyer stops buying, no matter how good the deal looks.
segments.tr: Nếu con số đó bằng không, người mua ngừng mua, bất kể thỏa thuận trông như thế nào.

segments.src: That is the whole point of the tool.
segments.tr: Đó là toàn bộ ý nghĩa của công cụ này.

segments.src: **Buying** is the execution: choosing vendors, negotiating cost and payment terms, setting order quantities and delivery dates, and deciding what share goes to national brands versus the retailer's own **private label**.
segments.tr: **Buying** là thực thi: chọn nhà cung cấp, đàm phán chi phí và điều khoản thanh toán, đặt số lượng đơn hàng và ngày giao hàng, và quyết định phần nào được phân bổ cho các thương hiệu quốc gia so với **private label** của nhà bán lẻ.

segments.src: Buyers are usually judged on two numbers rather than sales alone:
segments.tr: Người mua thường được đánh giá dựa trên hai con số thay vì chỉ doanh thu:

segments.src: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost
segments.tr: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold / Average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost
segments.tr: GMROI             = Gross margin dollars / Average inventory cost

segments.src: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") answers the question that actually matters: for every dollar tied up in inventory, how many gross margin dollars came back?
segments.tr: GMROI ("gross margin return on inventory investment") trả lời câu hỏi thực sự quan trọng: với mỗi đô la bị buộc trong hàng tồn kho, bao nhiêu đô la lợi nhuận gộp trở lại?

segments.src: A 20% margin item that sells eight times a year can beat a 45% margin item that sells twice.
segments.tr: Một mặt hàng với lợi nhuận 20% bán được tám lần một năm có thể vượt qua một mặt hàng có lợi nhuận 45% bán được hai lần.

segments.src: Margin alone is a half-answer.
segments.tr: Chỉ có lợi nhuận là một câu trả lời không hoàn chỉnh.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Compare two grocery runs.
segments.tr: So sánh hai lần đi mua sắm tạp hóa.

segments.src: At a conventional US supermarket — a Kroger, a Safeway, a big-format store — the peanut butter set might run 40 feet with 60-plus SKUs: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, the store brand, three organic options, powdered peanut butter, and a dozen sizes.
segments.tr: Tại một siêu thị truyền thống Mỹ — một Kroger, một Safeway, một cửa hàng định dạng lớn — kệ bơ lạc có thể kéo dài 40 feet với 60 cộng SKU: Jif, Skippy, Peter Pan, nhãn hiệu cửa hàng, ba tùy chọn hữu cơ, bơ lạc bột, và nhiều kích cỡ.

segments.src: Broad *and* deep.
segments.tr: Rộng *và* sâu.

segments.src: The store is making a promise: whatever you came for, we have it.
segments.tr: Cửa hàng đang đưa ra một lời hứa: bất kỳ thứ gì bạn đến tìm, chúng tôi đều có.

segments.src: At Trader Joe's, the same trip gives you a handful of options, mostly their own label.
segments.tr: Tại Trader Joe's, cùng một chuyến đi cho bạn một số ít tùy chọn, hầu hết là nhãn hiệu riêng của họ.

segments.src: The chain carries only a few thousand SKUs company-wide, where a full-size supermarket carries tens of thousands.
segments.tr: Chuỗi chỉ mang theo một vài nghìn SKU trên toàn công ty, trong khi một siêu thị kích thước đầy đủ mang theo hàng chục nghìn.

segments.src: That is not an oversight.
segments.tr: Đó không phải một sơ suất.

segments.src: Fewer SKUs means bigger orders per item, better cost per unit, faster turns, less shelf space wasted on slow movers, and a shopper who spends 20 minutes in the store instead of 45.
segments.tr: Ít SKU hơn có nghĩa là đơn hàng lớn hơn mỗi mặt hàng, chi phí tốt hơn mỗi đơn vị, quay vòng nhanh hơn, ít không gian kệ lãng phí cho những mặt hàng chuyển động chậm, và một người mua sắm chi tiêu 20 phút trong cửa hàng thay vì 45.

segments.src: Neither is "right."
segments.tr: Cái nào cũng không "đúng".

segments.src: They are different bets on the same two dials.
segments.tr: Chúng là những cược khác nhau trên cùng hai yếu tố.

segments.src: And you can watch the planning calendar in real time: the back-to-school endcaps that appear in July were bought in **February**, from a forecast written the previous fall.
segments.tr: Và bạn có thể xem lịch lập kế hoạch trong thời gian thực: các endcap quay lại trường học xuất hiện vào tháng Bảy được mua vào **tháng Hai**, từ một dự báo viết vào mùa thu trước.

segments.src: When you see backpacks at 60% off on Labor Day weekend, you are seeing a **markdown** — the planner's estimate was too high, and the store is converting dead inventory back into cash so the OTB refills for holiday.
segments.tr: Khi bạn thấy các ba lô được giảm 60% vào cuối tuần Ngày Lao động, bạn đang nhìn thấy một **markdown** — ước tính của nhà lập kế hoạch quá cao, và cửa hàng đang chuyển đổi hàng tồn kho chết thành tiền mặt để OTB được bổ sung lại cho kỳ nghỉ.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt Ba Dòng

segments.src: 1. Assortment is breadth (how many categories) times depth (how many choices per category) — that mix defines what kind of retailer you are.
segments.tr: 1. Assortment là breadth (bao nhiêu danh mục) nhân với depth (bao nhiêu lựa chọn mỗi danh mục) — hỗn hợp đó xác định bạn là loại nhà bán lẻ nào.

segments.src: 2. Merchandise planning turns a sales forecast into an inventory plan and an open-to-buy budget that caps what the buyer can commit.
segments.tr: 2. Merchandise planning chuyển đổi dự báo bán hàng thành một kế hoạch hàng tồn kho và ngân sách open-to-buy giới hạn những gì người mua có thể cam kết.

segments.src: 3. Buyers win on GMROI and turnover, not gross margin alone — a fast, thin-margin item can out-earn a slow, fat-margin one.
segments.tr: 3. Người mua thắng về GMROI và quay vòng, chứ không phải chỉ lợi nhuận gộp — một mặt hàng nhanh với lợi nhuận mỏng có thể kiếm được nhiều hơn một mặt hàng chậm với lợi nhuận cao.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Tự Kiểm Tra
